title: FizzBuzz
source: canonical FizzBuzz concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an integer n. Return a list holding one string for every integer from 1 to n, in order. For the value i: if i is divisible by both 3 and 5 the string is "FizzBuzz"; if it is divisible by 3 the string is "Fizz"; if it is divisible by 5 the string is "Buzz"; otherwise the string is the decimal representation of i.

examples.explanation: 3 is divisible by 3, 5 is divisible by 5, and no number in this range is divisible by 15.
15 is divisible by both 3 and 5, so its entry is "FizzBuzz".

hints: Walk the integers 1 through n once and decide each entry on its own before moving on.
One value can satisfy several divisibility rules at once. Which check must run first so that 15 does not come out as plain "Fizz"?
For each i, test i % 15 == 0 first and append "FizzBuzz"; then test i % 3 == 0, then i % 5 == 0; in every other case append str(i).
solution: One pass over 1..n with the divisibility checks ordered from most specific to least: divisible by 15, then by 3, then by 5, otherwise the number itself. Each entry is decided in constant time, so the whole list takes O(n) time and O(1) extra space beyond the output.
failureHint: hidden tests include n = 1, multiples of 15, and a large n
